purpose: Start a Region II inland-water source inventory that expands beyond the Cagayan B0380 basin and separates rivers, natural lakes, reservoirs, small water impounding projects, irrigation structures, aquaculture and fishery observations.

regionScope.name: Cagayan Valley / Region II
regionScope.coverageWarning: This is a first source-discovery tranche, not a complete regional waterbody or fish inventory. The Cagayan Riverine Zone plan excludes the northeast/northwest Cagayan watersheds that do not drain through the Cagayan River and eastern Isabela watersheds that drain to the Pacific. B0380 therefore cannot stand in for all Region II inland waters.

bfar2022AnnualReport.finding: The report lists Magat Dam and Reservoir and Cagayan River as inland resources; reports a 4,500-hectare Magat reservoir, 450 hectares allowed for fish cages, 183 operators, 1,415 cages, and 83,927 square metres under cages; lists Cagayan River length as 520 km and area as 3,030 hectares; and gives regional aggregate counts for 174 small water impounding projects and 25 diversion dams.
limits: The report does not define the method or geometry behind the Cagayan River area figure.
The 174 impounding projects and 25 diversion dams are aggregate counts, not individually named waterbodies or fish localities.
Fish-cage statistics describe aquaculture infrastructure, not wild-fish abundance or occurrence.
The report also reports freshwater fishponds and small farm reservoirs in its aquaculture section; these must remain separate from natural lake and river coverage.

bfar2018NifepAnnualReport.finding: The NIFEP section names Region II lakes, reservoirs and SWIPs as restoration/enhancement sites or 2018 target sites. It describes habitat restoration and a general stock-enhancement approach, but does not provide site-specific fish checklists or identify which named site received which fish stock.
limits: The 2018 sites are explicitly targets; this source alone does not verify completion.
Program-level mention of tilapia fingerlings for man-made reservoirs cannot be assigned to a named waterbody or treated as a wild occurrence.

niaMagatPages.finding: NIA-MARIIS identifies Magat Reservoir as part of the Cagayan River basin irrigation system and reports a 45-square-kilometre reservoir surface area at full supply level (193 m), compared with 15 square kilometres at the page's listed MSL (160 m). The full-supply figure converts to 4,500 hectares, numerically matching BFAR's 2022 reservoir-area figure.
limits: The matching area figures do not supply a downloadable reservoir polygon or the seasonal shoreline geometry.
This is water-infrastructure metadata, not a fish survey or permission to fish.

cagayanRiverinePlan.finding: The regional plan names the Cagayan River and major tributaries Addalam, Magat, Ilagan, Siffu-Mallig, Dummun, Pared, Pinacanauan and Chico, and explicitly says its study area excludes northeast/northwest Cagayan watersheds that do not drain through the Cagayan River and eastern Isabela watersheds draining to the Pacific.
limits: This is a 2005-2030 planning source; it is a system-level context, not a current hydrographic inventory or source of fish records.
The major-tributary list does not enumerate all tributaries, lakes, wetlands, reservoirs or local waterbody boundaries.

existingFishSurveyLead.scope: The review combines an NFRDI article on 2021 catches and 2020–2021 barangay production across three named Baggao sanctuaries with a 2018–2020 peer-reviewed telemetry study of two Hot Springs and Duba protected-area reaches near Pared River headwaters. The NFRDI labels are mostly genus-level; the telemetry study reports historical eel species evidence but no current or whole-river checklist.
existingFishSurveyLead.disposition: Keep survey, telemetry, NIFEP restoration-site names and B0380 basin geometry distinct. The Hot Springs/Duba cross-source site match remains unverified. No new public species, occurrence, or geometry rows are created.

siteLeads: Lake Bayo / Bayo Lake / Bayolake, Iguig
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: BFAR NIFEP program leads cross-checked with non-fish locality evidence and bounded fish-source searches. Casili/Cassily is plausible but unconfirmed; Bayo/Bayolake is a likely report spelling variant. No site-specific fish survey or checklist was retrieved; zero GBIF exact-text results do not prove absence.

siteLeads: Quirino General High School Reservoir, Cabarroguis
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: The Diffun QSU reservoir is a strong probable crosswalk to the 2015 NIFEP Quirino Reservoir lead; BFAR reports 5,000 fingerlings of unspecified carp species and tilapia stocked in 2016. This is a culture-based stocking record, not wild fish presence. The separate Cabarroguis high-school reservoir remains a 2018 target with completion and fish data unverified.

siteLeads: Magat Reservoir / Magat Dam Reservoir, Isabela–Ifugao boundary area
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: NAST sources report historical open-water catch labels and landings (1987–1988 and 1984–1991); ISU reports a 2022 Clarias gariepinus sample-study lead with wild-versus-cage origin unresolved. BFAR cage and unread production-spreadsheet data remain separate from wild observations. NIA and NAST reservoir area/depth values conflict and need reconciliation.

siteLeads: Potential ludong river-fishing leads in Ilagan, Maconacon, Palanan and Tumauini
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: The Isabela ENRO report gives 20 municipal count rows, including duplicate Jones and San Mariano submissions without explanation, and three dated Abuan water-monitoring stations. A DOST magazine lists potential ludong grounds but supplies no fish-site survey; one locality conflicts internally. These are waterbody and research leads only.

A 2020 household resource-use article abstract lists river-product labels attributed to Bintacan River, including tilapia and several unresolved local terms. It is not a fish survey; dates, scientific identities, vouchers and precise capture locations are unavailable in the abstract.

siteLeads: Kayaywan Lake / Itbayat freshwater lake; source spelling and provincial lake crosswalk unresolved
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: BFAR reports a tilapia cage-culture demonstration and 312 kg four-month managed harvest at Kayaywan Lake; its 2024 Batanes profile lists one unnamed 22-ha lake. PIA reports an Itbayat hatchery beside an unnamed freshwater lake in Reale. These do not establish wild fish presence, natural lake stocking, or a verified shoreline identity.

siteLeads: Buguey Lagoon, Cagayan; Villa Leonora, Centro and Cabaritan study-site leads
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: A 2026 CSU brief reports 56 finfish species and names a few, while a 2024 article from the same author has similar sites/method but no checklist or field-date range. A search-indexed 2015 abstract reports 43 finfish plus crustaceans, but its primary PDF and site list remain unavailable. The campaign crosswalk, taxon spellings, reuse rights and lagoon geometry remain unresolved.

siteLeads: North Luzon rivers and market/landing sites in Aurora, Cagayan and Zambales; one Cagayan site table label is ‘Buguey’ and type ‘river’
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: The 2025 peer-reviewed paper reports 1,513 vouchers and 323 species across three provinces and 27 mixed market/landing and river sites. Its supplementary XLSX with specimen, species, sampling-area, date and collection-method fields was retrieved, but no Cagayan specimen row uses ‘Buguey’ as its sampling-area label. The article's Buguey river site therefore has no resolved voucher/taxon crosswalk; article reuse terms are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and supplement/data rights need separate review.

siteLeads: Hot Springs freshwater protected area near Pared River headwaters; exact administrative crosswalk unverified
Duba freshwater protected area near Pared River headwaters; exact administrative crosswalk unverified
siteSpecificEvidenceReviews.finding: A 2022 peer-reviewed study sampled the two named protected-area reaches from 2018-03-29 through 2020-05-18 and reports eel catches were almost exclusively Anguilla marmorata, with two Anguilla bicolor encountered. This is historical reach-specific research evidence, not a current checklist; site-name/barangay matching and item-specific reuse terms remain open.

priorityFollowUps.task: Resolve whether NIFEP Piat Lake refers to Mapannao Lake or another site and seek a site-specific assessment. For Bangagalo/Bangalao, verify the historical table's vouchers, taxonomy, post-restoration stocking context and reuse terms, seek current monitoring and a reusable shoreline polygon. For Casili Lake and Bayolake, obtain separate dated site-specific surveys, methods, vouchers and usable geometry.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: Piat and Mapannao are not crosswalked by municipality alone. Bangalao's 2017–2018 landed catch table is not a current/resident checklist; the source does not distinguish stocked fish, and it cannot be transferred to Casili or Bayolake.

priorityFollowUps.task: Crosswalk the named Quirino reservoirs and SWIPs with current LGU/NIA/BFAR sources; confirm exact names, status, boundaries and whether each is a natural lake, man-made reservoir or irrigation impoundment.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: Regional aggregate SWIP counts do not identify individual sites or their fish assemblages.

priorityFollowUps.task: For Magat Reservoir, retrieve the original de los Triños 1993 proceedings chapter, Ortiz thesis and BFAR 2019–2022 production spreadsheet; reconcile the NAST/NIA area and depth conflict; seek a recent standardized open-water fish survey and a stage-aware reusable shoreline source. Keep cages and aquaculture separate from wild catch.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: Historical catch shares, cage counts, farmed production, contaminant-study samples or reservoir size do not establish current wild presence, abundance, safety, catchability, or a fixed shoreline.

priorityFollowUps.task: Crosswalk Isabela's municipality-submitted wetland counts to named rivers, lakes, SWIPs, reservoirs and wetlands and to official feature maps. Resolve duplicate Jones/San Mariano rows; for Batanes, confirm the Kayaywan/unnamed-lake name and geometry and seek a wild-fish survey. Then continue with the northeast/northwest Cagayan watersheds outside the Cagayan Riverine Zone.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: The Cagayan River basin polygon is not a Region II inland-water boundary. Municipal counts, DOST's possible ludong-fishing-ground labels, household resource-use lists, aquaculture and provincial lake-area totals do not establish named wild species occurrences or feature geometry.

priorityFollowUps.task: For Buguey Lagoon, obtain the full 2015 Urmeneta/Romias proceedings or checklist and the complete dataset behind CSU's 56-fin-fish 2026 brief; resolve its relationship to Pascua (2024), field dates, station/taxon crosswalk, source spellings, vouchers, reuse terms, and official lagoon geometry. Then continue the northeast, northwest and Pacific-draining Cagayan watersheds outside the Cagayan Riverine Zone.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: The 2015 abstract is search-indexed only and reports 43 finfishes; the 2026 brief reports 56 but does not publish a full checklist. Do not merge their counts or names, infer a current species inventory, promote a protected-area recommendation as enacted law, or infer water quality or safety.

priorityFollowUps.task: Ask the corresponding author to reconcile the article's main-table Buguey river site with the retrieved supplementary Tables S1a–S1c: no Cagayan specimen row uses Buguey as a sampling-area label. Clarify whether no sequenced specimens came from that site or whether another sampling-area label was used; obtain explicit rights terms before reusing any site/specimen data. Then continue site-by-site research for northeast/northwest Cagayan and Pacific-draining Isabela watersheds.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: The aggregate 323-species count is not a checklist for any single province or site. Do not treat market fish as local wild occurrences, join generic or differently named Cagayan river rows to the Buguey point, map it to Buguey Lagoon, or adapt/re-publish CC BY-NC-ND material without an explicit rights decision.

priorityFollowUps.task: For the Pared River eel telemetry lead, verify with the authors, BFAR/LGU, or primary site records whether the Hot Springs and Duba FPAs in the 2022 study are exactly the Baggao Hot Spring (Asinga-Via) and Duba Cave (San Miguel) sites. Confirm the article's item-specific Open Access license and seek current, site-resolved fish monitoring plus authoritative protected-area boundaries and rules before any public use.
priorityFollowUps.doNotInfer: The 2018–2020 telemetry catches do not establish current presence, river-wide distribution, a complete checklist, fishing permission, or sanctuary boundaries. Do not copy the study's coordinates or infer barangays from similar site names.
